text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwean press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Zimbabwe could lose more than Z$5 million of its investment in the Nairobi-based Preferential Trade Area Bank if the institution, embroiled in a major financial scandal, is allowed to collapse.

- Enhanced Communications Network, which last week lost a bid to operate Zimbabwe's second cellular phone service, is reported to have attempted to strike a deal with the winning tenderer Telecel to help it secure a third operating licence.
- The World Bank said on Wednesday it would assess the country's 1997/98 budget before deciding on the release of a second tranche of U.S.$62.5 million to support Zimbabwe's balance of payments.

- A deal in which horticultural producers and processers Interfresh (Pvt) Ltd will seek a listing on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange through a reverse takeover of listed fine paper manufacturers Kadoma Consolidated Industries, is close to being finalised.
- Central African Building Society is to cut interest rates payable on various mortgage loans with effect from April.
- Zimbabwean importers hit hard by a new tariff system have accused the Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries of betrayal, saying it did not put forward to government tariff proposals.
- The World Bank has committed Z$1.1 billion to support Zimbabwe's poverty alleviation programme.
- British and French business are eager to invest in Zimbabwe and the government will expedite the processing of their applications, President Robert Mugabe said in Harare.
